criteria.criterion: Root cause is named in the CHANGELOG.md entry and in a doc comment: reading output was checked only for prior-result, evidence, survey and governance rules, not against the boundary word list or repo files at HEAD. The check is called from check_reading_acceptance in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, not in a prompt file.
criteria.evidence: CHANGELOG.md entry: "Root cause: a reading was checked only for the previous result and change scope, the evidence each criterion rests on, the code survey and the governance files. Nothing compared its text with the boundary word list or its deliverables with the files at the base commit". The doc comment on check_boundary_and_repo_files (reading.rs ~2326) says the same. check_reading_acceptance (reading.rs 2419-2431) ends with `check_boundary_and_repo_files(reading, repo_files)`. `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` shows no prompt file changed.

criteria.criterion: A unit test in reading.rs fails without the change and passes with it: a reading whose summary holds a boundary-scan word is refused and the error names the word. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.
criteria.evidence: reading::tests::a_reading_whose_summary_holds_a_boundary_word_is_refused_and_the_word_is_named passed. So did a_boundary_word_in_any_text_field_or_path_is_refused_with_the_field_named. summary: The change passes. It adds `check_boundary_and_repo_files` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and calls it last from `check_reading_acceptance`. The check runs every text field and every deliverable path of a reading through the existing `boundary_scan`. Given the file list at the base commit (`git ls-tree -r` on the job's commit), it also refuses a modify or delete of an absent path and a create of an existing file. The refusal names the field, word or path and goes back to the reader as its one correction. I read the diff and ran `cargo test -p athena-core reading` (110 passed, including 5 new unit tests and 3 new reader-path tests) and `cargo test -p athena-core` (613 passed, 1 ignored). I also ran the new fake-reader test in athena-agent, which passed. For fmt, clippy and the full test suite I cite Athena's recorded passes. The CHANGELOG entry and the doc comment both name the root cause and state the 5% estimate as intended and not measured. No prompt file changed. Two kinds of minor finding. First, scope: test files outside the expected-deliverables list changed: run_pin_tests.rs, fake.rs, drain.rs and steward.rs. steward.rs was not even in the planned files. Each change is a test or fixture fix the new rule needs. Second, the measured replay checks only the words: the replay passes no file list, so the path rule's refusal rate is untested.
